status: Fixed in source; frozen runner publication remains
area: Task claim ownership / lane session diagnostics
finding: ATM_TASK_CLAIM_OWNER_MISMATCH originally decided ownership on lane session ids but rendered its message from actor ids. The message seam was repaired first. A second defect then remained: same-actor next --claim and renew flows could mint a fresh lane before comparing it with the active claim, producing ATM_LOCK_CONFLICT even though the actor was unchanged. The repair binds an idempotent same-actor flow to the active claim's holding lane; a different actor still presents its own lane and remains a conflict.
expectedBehavior: The mismatch message must name whichever identity actually discriminated. In lane-id mode it must name the holding lane and the requested lane, and when both sides share one actor it must say so explicitly. An idempotent same-actor active-claim flow must reuse the holding lane rather than minting a competing lane; a different actor must preserve the existing conflict behaviour. In actor-fallback mode the existing actor wording remains byte-for-byte stable.
evidenceOrRepro: Reproduced five times on 2026-08-25 across TASK-PRF-0002 and TASK-PRF-0004 during Product Proof parallel-claim runs. Source repair is covered by tests/cli/claim-owner-mismatch-message.test.ts, tests/cli/lane-claim-conflict-matrix.test.ts, and tests/cli/tasks-claim-auto-intent.test.ts: same actor with holding lane lane-holding resolves to that lane, a different actor retains lane-fresh, and a real task renew preserves the original claim lane without a fresh-lane conflict.
followUp: The same-actor lane re-claim defect and the adjacent explicit next --task routing defect are resolved in source. Frozen runner publication remains pending because the packaged runner is stale; formal backlog closeout follows runner publication.
